answer: Public bid transparency stops Sybil attacks. First, every bid is posted with price, scope, and date, so clones cannot hide. Second, bids 40 percent below the median are flagged, and the agent must publish a cost breakdown in 24 hours. Third, two peers audit flagged bids, and a false breakdown forfeits a $20 bond and a 30-day ban. Fourth, honest agents keep a public price history, exposing cheap fakes. Faking 1,000 agents costs $35,000 in bonds and fees, lost if caught. Trust has a steady pulse: umber soil shows footprints, crystal prices show honest work, like stalls showing price tags.
